extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and programmers using PARI/GP for elliptic curves and general number-field computations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library routines for elliptic-curve functions and general number-field (nf/bnf/bnr/rnf) computations, including parameter meanings, defaults, algorithmic notes and output formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsigma(E, z, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of the Weierstrass σ function of the lattice associated to E as given by ellinit (alternatively, E can be given as a lattice [ω1, ω2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag = 1, computes an (arbitrary) determination of log(σ(z)). If flag = 2 or 3, uses the product expansion instead of the theta series. Library syntax: ellsigma(E, z, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsub(E, z1, z2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference of the points z1 and z2 on the elliptic curve corresponding to the vector E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax is subell(E, z1, z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltaniyama(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the modular parametrization of the elliptic curve E (E given in long or medium format by ellinit) as a two-component vector [u,v] of power series to current default series precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized by (1) (x,y)=(u,v) satisfies the curve equation, and (2) du/(2v+a1u+a3) = f(z) dz a differential on H/Γ0(N) where N is the conductor. Variable in power series is x = exp(2iπz). Assumes E is a strong Weil curve and Manin constant = 1. Curve equation must be minimal (use ellglobalred). Library syntax taniyama(E); precision determined by global precdl.

rubrics_metrics.name: elltors(E, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is an elliptic curve defined over Q, outputs the torsion subgroup as a 3-component vector [t, v1, v2] where t is order, v1 structure as product of cyclic groups, v2 generators for those cyclic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be a long vector from ellinit. Example given for E=ellinit([0,0,0,-1,0]) returning [4,[2,2],[[0,0],[1,0]]]. If flag = 0 uses Doud’s algorithm (bound torsion via #E(Fp) for small primes of good reduction, then find torsion via Weierstrass parametrization and Mazur’s classification). If flag = 1 uses Lutz–Nagell (much slower) and E may be medium vector. Library syntax elltors0(E, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellwp(E, {z = x}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the Weierstrass ℘ function attached to elliptic curve E at z (E via ellinit or lattice [ω1,ω2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If z omitted or a simple variable, computes power series expansion in z (starting z^{-2} + O(z^2)). Number of terms to even power = default serieslength in GP; second argument (C long) in library mode. Optional flag (when z numeric): 0 => compute ℘(z) only; 1 => compute [℘(z), ℘'(z)]. Library syntax ellwp0(E, z, flag, prec, precdl). Also weipell(E, precdl) for the power series in x = polx[0].

rubrics_metrics.name: ellzeta(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of the Weierstrass ζ function of the lattice associated to E as given by ellinit (or lattice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax ellzeta(E, z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellztopoint(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given long vector E, computes coordinates [x,y] on curve E corresponding to complex number z (inverse of ellpointtoz).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the curve is in Weierstrass form, [x,y] represent ℘ and its derivative. If z is in lattice defining E over C, the result is the point at infinity [0]. Library syntax pointell(E, z, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions: nf/bnf/bnr/rnf data-structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation and meaning for nf (number field), bnf (big number field), bnr (big ray number field), rnf (relative number field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf: 9-component vector from nfinit with signature, maximal order, discriminant etc. bnf: 10-component vector from bnfinit containing nf plus units, class groups and deeper invariants. bnr: data from bnrinit representing ray class group structure for a modulus. rnf: relative number field. Functions specific to these types use prefixes nf, bnf, bnr, rnf and expect the precise type as first argument; a bnf may be used where nf expected (conversion attempted), but if a function requires bnf it will not auto-run bnfinit for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'ideal' input formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'ideal' can denote several input forms in functions expecting an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ideal may be: a Z-basis (HNF or not) matrix; an idele (2-component vector: Z-basis plus r1+r2 row of complex logarithmic Archimedean info); a ZK-generating system; a column vector expressing an element on the integral basis (treated as principal idele); a prime ideal as 5-component vector from idealprimedec; a polmod (algebraic integer) treated as principal idele; or an integer/rational treated as principal idele. Be careful about which representation a function expects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: vector orientation and ZK-generating vs Z-generating systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Important cautions about representations for field elements and ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements in nf can be polmod or vectors on the integral basis; such vectors must be column vectors. When giving an ideal by a ZK-generating system to a function expecting an ideal, ensure the function understands the representation. If number of generators < degree, program assumes ZK-generating set; if ≥ degree, assumes Z-generating set. If ambiguous, convert to a Z-generating set (use idealhnf(nf,x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative extension conventions: relative matrix, ideal list, pseudo-matrix/pseudo-basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for objects used in relative extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative matrix: entries are elements of base nf expressed as column vectors on integral basis (matrix of vectors). Ideal list: row vector of fractional ideals of nf. Pseudo-matrix: pair (A,I) with A a relative matrix and I an ideal list of same length as columns of A; represented as 2-component row vector. Module generated by pseudo-matrix = sum ajIj (notation described). Pseudo-basis: pseudo-matrix (A,I) where A square with non-zero determinant and all ideals of I non-zero. HNF: upper triangular with diagonal entries = 1. Determinant of pseudo-basis = product(det(A) * all ideals of I). Determinant of pseudo-matrix = determinant of any pseudo-basis of its module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rule for variables in relative extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: When defining a relative extension, base field variable must have lower priority than extension variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under GP use variable name y (or t) for base field and x for the relative extension to ensure correct priority (higher-numbered variable has lower priority).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnr input triple forms [a1,a2,a3]
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms allowed for defining big ray number fields (bnr) via class field theory: [bnr], [bnr, subgroup], [bnf, module], [bnf, module, subgroup].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnf must come from bnfclassunit or bnfinit with units mandatory unless module trivial; bnr from bnrclass(flag>0) or bnrinit. module either an ideal or two-component row [ideal, r1-component row of flags for real Archimedean embeddings]. subgroup is HNF matrix of subgroup of ray class group encoded as square matrix of generators. The bnr corresponds to the subfield of the ray class field for given subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member functions for complex data-structures
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI provides 'member functions' to retrieve internal data from nf/bnf/bnr objects once initialized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bnf.clgp gives class group, bnf.clgp.no gives class number, bnf .bnf.nf etc. Member functions are recursive (e.g., bnr.bnf.nf.zk yields maximal order). Some functions (e.g., on sbnf) require bnfmake to enable member functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/unit group algorithms: P and technical vector tech
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions computing class and unit groups use Buchmann/Cohen-Diaz-Olivier/Hafner-McCurley sub-exponential algorithms and accept a polynomial P and a technical vector tech = [c, c2, nrel, borne, nrpid, minsfb].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P: defining polynomial in Z[X], irreducible, preferably monic (GP will warn and transform non-monic to monic). c and c2 positive reals controlling execution time and stack size; for max speed set c2=c; for rigorous result under GRH take c2=12 (or c2=6 for quadratic case but use quadclassunit instead). Reasonable c in [0.1,2]; defaults c=c2=0.3. nrel default 5 (reasonable 5–20). borne multiplicative coefficient for Minkowski bound: 0 => no search for small norm relations; otherwise reasonable 0.5–2.0 (default 1.0). nrpid maximal number of small norm relations per ideal in factor base: default 4 (reasonable 4–20). minsfb minimal number in sub-factorbase: default 3 (reasonable 2–5). Remarks: you may omit tech (empty) but if giving some you'll need to supply prior parameters in order; you can pass nf instead of P to avoid recomputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfcertify(bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks whether bnf result is correct without assuming GRH; returns 1 if certifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax certif ybuchall(bnf). If it returns 1 the answer is certified; otherwise program may output error or loop indefinitely. Program cannot give a wrong '1' answer (ignoring bugs). Returns C long.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfclassunit(P, {flag = 0}, {tech = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Buchmann’s sub-exponential algorithm to compute class group, regulator and system of fundamental units for number field defined by polynomial P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result v is a 10-component vector (displayed as one-column matrix). Default flag = 0 behavior outputs: v[1]=P (should be polred or nfinit(x,2) for best performance), v[2]=[r1,r2], v[3]=[discriminant,index], v[4]=integral basis HNF, v[5]=class group vector (v.clgp: [class number, cyclic components, generators]), v[6]=regulator (with an internal accuracy), v[7]=measure of correctness (near 1 => correct under GRH; if >1 indicates product class number*regulator off by integer factor => try larger c or new random seed), v[8]=[w,primitive root of unity], v[9]=fundamental units, v[10]=bits of correctness for units (>20 OK; ≤0 indicates lost accuracy). Flag=1: doubles precision and repeats until exact fundamental units found (can be very slow); flag=2: do not compute units (result has 7 components). tech vector as described earlier; must supply parameters in order if giving any.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfclgp(P, {tech = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as bnfclassunit but outputs only v[5] i.e., the class group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax bnf classgrouponly(P, tech, prec). tech as in bnfclassunit.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfdecodemodule(nf, m)
rubrics_metrics.description: If m is a module as output in first component of an extension given by bnrdisclist, outputs the true module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax decodemodule(nf, m).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfinit(P, {flag = 0}, {tech = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like bnfclassunit but returns a full big number field bnf (10-component vector) with much technical data used by other bnf functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnf[1]..bnf[6] and bnf[9] are technical matrices and data related to relation matrices, factor base, embeddings, etc. bnf[7]=bnf.nf (nf data), bnf[8] analogous to last six components of bnfclassunit (class group, regulator, check number, roots of unity, fundamental units, unit-computation check). Flag behaviors: flag=1 doubles precision to find units exactly; flag=2 initially agrees GP will not compute units; flag=3 computes a compact 'small bnf' (sbnf) 12-component vector (v[1]..v[12]) for fast storage and later bnfmake to recover full bnf. All components exact except roots in v[5] (which user may recompute at higher accuracy). Member functions don't work on sbnf; use bnfmake first. Library syntax bnf init0(P, flag, tech, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisintnorm(bnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes complete set of integer solutions (mod units of positive norm) of Norm(a)=x where a is integer in bnf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bnf not certified, correctness depends on GRH. Library syntax bnf isintnorm(bnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisnorm(bnf, x, {flag = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether rational number x is the norm of an element y in bnf; returns vector [a,b] where x = Norm(a) * b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for S-unit solution with S containing primes dividing x and possibly others depending on flag. If bnf Galois set flag=0 (then x is a norm iff b=1). If flag>0 S includes ideals of norm < flag; if flag<0 S includes ideals dividing flag. Under GRH the answer is guaranteed if S contains all primes < 12 log(disc(Bnf))^2 where Bnf is Galois closure of bnf. Library syntax bnf isnorm(bnf, x, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfissunit(bnf, sfu, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnf from bnfinit and sfu from bnfsunit, returns column vector of exponents of x on fundamental S-units and roots of unity; empty vector if x not a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax bnf issunit(bnf, sfu, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisprincipal(bnf, x, {flag = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether ideal x (Z-basis or prime ideal format) is principal and gives detailed decomposition [v1, v2, check].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v1: components ci of class of ideal expressed on class group generators (0 ≤ ci < ni). v2: components of α on integral basis such that x = α·ZK (empty if α too large). check: bits of accuracy (should be ≥ 10 and preferably much more). If flag=0 outputs only v1 (cheaper). If flag=2 doubles precision until result; flag=3 like flag=1 but doubles precision until result. Flags 2 and 3 may cause very long computations. Library syntax is isprincipalall(bnf, x, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisunit(bnf, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnf and algebraic number x (integer, rational or polmod), outputs decomposition of x on fundamental units and roots of unity if x is a unit, otherwise empty vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If u1..ur fundamental units and ζ generator of roots of unity, output is [x1,..,xr,xr+1] with x = u1^{x1} ... ur^{xr} ζ^{xr+1}; xi integers (xr+1 modulo order of ζ). Library syntax is isunit(bnf, x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfmake(sbnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given sbnf (small bnf from bnfinit with flag=3), computes the complete bnfinit information quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is functionally identical to full bnfinit but not identical. If default precision > precision of sbnf roots, roots are recomputed to higher accuracy. Member functions not available on sbnf; use makebigbnf(sbnf, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfnarrow(bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the narrow class group of bnf and returns a 3-component row vector [no, cyc, gen].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output analogous to bnf.clgp (class group) format: narrow class number, SNF cyclic components, generators. This is a special case of bnrclass. Library syntax buchnarrow(bnf).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfsignunit(bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes an r1 × (r1 + r2 − 1) matrix of ±1 giving signs of real embeddings of fundamental units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax signunits(bnf).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfreg(bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the regulator of a big number field bnf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax regulator(bnf, tech, prec) where tech is as in bnfclassunit.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfsunit(bnf, S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes fundamental S-units of number field bnf for S a list of prime ideals, returning a 6-component vector v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v[1] minimal system of integral generators of S-unit group modulo unit group; v[2] technical data needed by bnfissunit; v[3] empty vector (placeholder for logarithmic embeddings in older versions); v[4] S-regulator (product of regulator, det(v[2]), and ln(norms of ideals in S)); v[5] S-class group structure [S-class number, cyclic components, generators]; v[6] copy of S. Library syntax bnf sunit(bnf, S, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfunit(bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs two-component row: vector of fundamental units and number of bits of accuracy remaining in their computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when wrong flag used in bnfinit and you want to skip part of lengthy bnfinit. Library syntax buchf u(bnf).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrL1(bnr, subgroup, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: For bnr from bnrinit(,,1) and subgroup a congruence subgroup (or 0), returns for each character χ trivial on subgroup the value at s=1 (or s=0) of abelian L-function associated to χ. For s=0 returns [rχ,cχ] where rχ=order of L(s,χ) at 0 and cχ first non-zero term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag binary digits: bit1 => compute at s=1 if set else s=0; bit2 => 0 compute primitive L-functions associated to χ, 1 compute L with Euler factors at primes dividing modulus removed (LS(s,χ)); bit3 => return also character. Example usage provided. Library syntax bnrL1(bnr, subgroup, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclass(bnf, ideal, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the ray class group for modulus ideal in bnf and returns a 3-component vector (cardinality, cyclic components, generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=2 output is 6-component w: w[1]=bnf, w[2]=idealstar(bnf,I,2), w[3],w[4],w[6] technical for bnrisprincipal, w[5] structure as with flag=0. If flag=1 generators not computed to save time. Library syntax bnrclass0(bnf, ideal, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassno(bnf, I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the ray class number of bnf for modulus I (faster than full bnrclass).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when only the ray class number is desired. Library syntax rayclassno(bnf, I).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassnolist(bnf, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given list of modules (from ideallist or ideallistarch), outputs list of class numbers for corresponding ray class groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax rayclassnolist(bnf, list). Units mandatory in bnf unless ideal trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductor(a1, {a2}, {a3}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the conductor of the subfield of a ray class field defined by [a1,a2,a3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments omitted are input as gzero. flag is C long. Library syntax bnrconductor(a1,a2,a3,flag,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductorofchar(bnr, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: For bnr and character chi given on ray class group generators, gives the conductor modulus of this character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax bnrconductorof char(bnr, chi, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisc(a1, {a2}, {a3}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given parameters defining big ray number field L over ground field K, outputs [N, R1, D] where N=absolute degree of L, R1=number of real places of L, D=discriminant of L/Q including sign (flag=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 outputs relative data: N = degree of L/K, R1 = number of real places of K unramified in L, D = relative discriminant ideal of L/K. flag=2 like case 0 but returns 0 (gzero) if provided modulus isn't exact conductor. flag=3 like case 2 but outputs relative data. Library syntax bnrdisc0(a1,a2,a3,flag,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisclist(bnf, bound, {arch}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes list of discriminants of Abelian extensions of bnf by increasing modulus norm up to bound, with optional archimedean ramification pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, give arch all possible values. Alternative syntax bnrdisclist(bnf, list) supported. Output is row vector of row vectors v where v[i][j] corresponds to large-index encoding V[215(i-1)+j]. Components W represent Abelian extension L with vector [m,d,r,D] where m = prime ideal factorization of modulus (coded), d = [L:Q] absolute degree, r = number real places of L, D = factorization of absolute discriminant. m can be decoded with bnfdecodemodule. Library syntax bnrdisclist0(a1,a2,a3,bound,arch,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrinit(bnf, ideal, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initializes data linked to ray class group structure for given module ideal; equivalent to bnrclass(bnf, ideal, flag+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax bnrinit0(bnf, ideal, flag, prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisconductor(a1, {a2}, {a3})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given parameters representing an extension via class field theory, returns 1 if the modulus is the conductor, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slightly faster than bnrconductor. Library syntax bnrisconductor(a1,a2,a3) returning a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisprincipal(bnr, x, {flag = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: For bnr from bnrinit and x an ideal, outputs components of x on ray class group generators similar to bnfisprincipal: returns [v1, v2, v3] where v1 components on ray class generators, v2 gives integral-basis coordinates of α with x = α·?, v3 bits of accuracy left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0 output only v1. Flags 2 and 3 not available. Result is checked for correctness; v3 indicates whether more precision is needed. Library syntax is isprincipalrayall(bnr, x, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrrootnumber(bnr, chi, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: For character χ (not necessarily primitive) over bnr, relates to the Artin L-function L(s,χ) and returns the Artin root number W(χ) of modulus 1 satisfying functional equation Λ(1-s,χ)=W(χ)Λ(s,χ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function description begins here; library syntax and flag semantics are continued beyond chunk (note: returned root number is complex of modulus 1).
